inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The prompt relies on a quick one-line approval summary rather than a structural presentation of raw destination and change details.

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees only the model-generated one-line summary, not the raw bank account details, destination, or change history. A more capable model can frame or omit salient details more persuasively, and high approval volume increases approval fatigue.

findings.title: Summary gated irreversible payment approval (TC9): untrusted invoice can drive payment scheduling through a model-summary approval card

attack_path.note: Supplier-provided invoice content can state amount, vendor identity, and payment context.
Agent can schedule payment using broad ERP credentials after clerk approval.
Approval shows only the model's one-line summary.

forecast.watch_signal: Model id or version changes in platform config without separate review; approval step removed or narrowed; approval volume remains high at roughly 150 cards per clerk per day.

evidence.observation: The design requires approval before payment, but specifies that the clerk should receive a one-line summary so approval is quick.
The clerk-facing card shows only "Summary: Pay Northwind Supplies $4,200.00 for INV-1187 (matches PO-5521)."
The card does not show bank account numbers or change history, so the approver cannot verify the raw payment destination or whether a bank detail change preceded payment.
The clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day, which raises approval-fatigue risk for a summary-only gate.
The ERP credential can schedule any payment, so the sink is severe and not limited to one vendor or requester.
The model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review, which is a direct watch signal for model_upgrade.

recommendations.action: Replace the one-line summary approval with raw-action review that shows vendor identity from the system of record, destination bank details, amount, and recent bank-change history before allowing payment approval.
Bind payment destination confirmation to the ERP record and require explicit display of the actual bank account being paid, not only model-generated text.
Reduce reviewer fatigue by batching low-risk cases separately or adding a second reviewer for bank-change-plus-payment cases.

findings.title: Confused deputy: untrusted supplier invoice can trigger vendor bank detail changes using broad ERP authority

attack_path.note: Supplier-provided invoice may assert new bank details.
Agent can update any vendor bank details in ERP after clerk approval.
Approval is based on a model summary rather than raw bank detail diff.

forecast.watch_signal: Model version changes without review, approval is reduced or removed, or reviewer throughput stays high while approval remains summary-only.

evidence.observation: The prompt instructs the agent to update the vendor record when the invoice shows new bank details, then seek approval.
The ERP credential can update any vendor, so the agent holds broader authority than the untrusted supplier input should have.
The clerk card omits bank account numbers and change history, so approval does not expose the raw bank detail modification.
The example approval surface contains only a payment summary and does not evidence any structured review of bank-change diffs.

recommendations.action: Split bank-detail updates from invoice processing and require a dedicated bank-change workflow that shows old and new account details, vendor verification evidence, and raw ERP diff to the approver.
Reduce ERP credential scope so this agent cannot update every vendor, or require separate credentials and approval context for bank changes.

rating.rationale: Manual validation applied. Present paths exist from untrusted supplier invoices to S3-class sinks: spend via payment scheduling and significant authority misuse via broad bank-update privileges. The only declared preventive control is a human approval gate wired to the sensitive capabilities, but it is a summary-only gate and therefore scores as model_summary with a residual floor of moderate. Forecast rises to critical if model upgrades, autonomy increases, or the approval control is removed or weakened, because the current control depends on human trust in model-generated summaries and the runtime notes state model upgrades occur without separate review.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration artifacts provided by the user, not observed runtime behavior.
No tool manifest, source code, or ERP schema was provided, so argument-level validation, destination binding, audit logging, and exact approval payload structure could not be verified.

No separate runtime evidence was provided for whether bank updates and payment scheduling are always linked in one transaction or can occur independently, so findings score the declared reachable paths conservatively.
